amendment_note: Amended before any SELECTED-SET outcome exists (handoff 239): (1) N set to 5,000 with the overfitting rationale; (2) a pilot-disclosure section added -- a cost measurement preceded and informed N; (3) the redraw/resize prohibition reworded to forbid resizing after the SELECTED SET's own outcomes are seen, not sizing from an independent pilot, which the earlier wording accidentally forbade; (4) a second selector test added, asserting the pilot artifacts are not selection inputs. Amended while stage 4 has still never run -- no outcome for any hash-selected curve exists.
status: FROZEN before any outcome for this window exists. Stage 4 (signature_inventory) has never run against B11a; no signature count, trade, graduation, price, or reserve has been observed for any curve in this cohort. This document is written into that clean state deliberately.

why_this_exists.the_scale_finding: The B11a cohort is 33,866 curves -- every Pump create in a 24h window, not a selected set. Stage 5 (transaction_bodies) fetches one getTransaction per signature. The pipeline was sized against the burned B9 study's ~59 signatures per curve; a direct measurement disproves that for this window.
why_this_exists.the_measurement_not_an_extrapolation: Curves drawn at random (fixed seeds 11/40 and 23/80 curves -- the cost pilot disclosed in full below) from the cohort, signatures counted at or below the observation cutoff: min 1, p25 2, MEDIAN 31, p75 2,178, max 11,102, MEAN 1,283. The mean is ~22x the burned study's figure, and the distribution is extremely heavy-tailed -- the median curve is quiet and a few carry thousands. These are AGGREGATES over random draws unrelated to this document's hash rule; the pilot never derived which curves the rule selects.
why_this_exists.the_projected_cost: 1,283 mean x 33,866 = ~43.4 million in-window signatures (the sample's own error puts it near +/- 9.1M). At the measured concurrent ceiling of 13.76 getTransaction/s (4 workers; 8 only reached 15.7 with the provider already queueing) that is ~36 days for stage 5, ~86 serial. No worker count closes it: a one-week stage needs ~72 calls/s, five times what the provider will serve this credential.
why_this_exists.the_conclusion: This is a SCALE problem, not a tuning one. The full cohort cannot be collected in a tractable time, and the earlier ~2.4-day estimate was an extrapolation of the burned per-curve rate onto a window ~22x more active per curve. The cohort must be subsampled, and the subsample must be chosen before any outcome is seen -- which, because stage 4 never ran, it can still be.

the_rule.frame: Every curve in research/b11a/b11a_cohort.sqlite, identified by its `mint` -- the stable creation identity, one row per curve, 33,866 rows. The frame is the whole cohort; nothing is pre-excluded.
the_rule.selection: A deterministic hash-threshold uniform sample. For each curve compute key = sha256(SEED || mint) as a big-endian integer; select the N curves with the SMALLEST key. This is a uniform random draw without replacement that is also reproducible from (SEED, N) and the cohort's mints alone.
the_rule.N_is_the_one_operational_knob: N is the only parameter that sets the sample's SIZE without changing the rule's structure. It controls HOW MANY curves are drawn, never WHICH -- the hash order fixes which, and N takes a prefix of that order. The owner set N=5,000.
the_rule.why_N_is_5000_the_overfitting_rationale: The failure that kills a trading strategy is not a slow start, it is an edge fitted to NOISE, and sample size is the direct defence. This data is hostile to small samples: median 31, max 11,102 signatures per curve, so a handful of curves dominate any statistic and a heavy tail needs MORE sample for the same confidence, not less. At ~600 active curves a couple of outliers can manufacture an apparent edge; at ~1,500 that is much harder. 5,000 is also the largest N that finishes stage 5 inside a week -- ~6.4M signatures, ~5.4 days at the measured rate -- and of those 5,000, on the pilot's distribution roughly 3,000 carry real history and ~1,500 are genuinely active. The owner chose the largest tractable N precisely so the frozen studies have the most defence against fitting the tail.
the_rule.why_hash_threshold_not_random_sample: A hash on the mint is reproducible, auditable and tamper-evident: anyone can recompute the exact selection from SEED, N and the cohort, and a changed SEED or N produces a visibly different set. `random.sample` leaves no such trail.
the_rule.nested_property_stated_for_honesty_not_u: Because selection is the N smallest hashes, a larger N is a SUPERSET of a smaller one: the sample for any N' < 5,000 is contained in the sample for N=5,000. This makes a staged approach POSSIBLE -- collect a smaller prefix first, and if the realised cost is low extend by collecting only the added curves. It is documented because it is a real property of the rule, but V1 fixes N at a single value; any staged extension is a SEPARATE preregistered decision, because letting realised cost choose the final N -- once the SELECTED SET's outcomes are visible -- is a dependency on the study's own results, and it should be entered deliberately rather than drifted into.

the_prohibition_this_document_exists_to_.no_selection_on_anything_downstream_of_l: The selection key is a function of `mint` and the frozen SEED ONLY. It reads NO signature count, trade count, graduation status, price, reserve, or any quantity produced after the curve was created. Those ARE the outcome; selecting on them is selecting on the dependent variable, and it is tempting precisely because dropping the quiet tokens is what would make collection cheap -- which is exactly why it is refused.
the_prohibition_this_document_exists_to_.creation_time_keys_are_the_only_legitima: What is known at t0 and MAY key a sample: a random draw (used here), launch_slot, is_mayhem_mode. What may NOT: everything the collection is being run to observe. The cohort table carries mint, bonding_curve, launch_slot, is_mayhem_mode, create_signature -- all creation-time -- and NO outcome column, so the rule cannot accidentally reach one.
the_prohibition_this_document_exists_to_.a_test_will_enforce_this: Two tests. (a) The selector implementation must take ONLY (mint, SEED, N) and a test asserts its inputs are creation-time identity, never an activity quantity -- read from the AST, the same way b16d's pricing function is proven not to read the creator's own flow. (b) A test asserts the pilot code (research/b11f/pilot/, see disclosure below) contains NO selection machinery AT ALL -- no executable pilot module imports hashlib or references sha256, the frozen SEED constant, or nsmallest-style hash ordering. This is the stronger form: asserting the absence of the machinery survives someone later adding a hash helper to a pilot script, whereas merely asserting 'the selector does not import the pilot' does not. NOTE the test scopes to the EXECUTABLE pilot modules (the .py files, AST-parsed): the README documents the property in prose and therefore contains the words sha256 and smallest, so a naive substring grep over the whole directory would trip on documentation -- the check is over code, not text.
the_prohibition_this_document_exists_to_.the_boundary_between_legitimate_sizing_a: SEED and N are frozen here. What is FORBIDDEN: redrawing, reseeding, or resizing once the SELECTED SET's OWN OUTCOMES are observed -- i.e. after stage 4+ has produced any signature count, trade, graduation, price or reserve for a curve the hash rule selects. Choosing N by looking at the study's own results is selecting on the dependent variable. What is LEGITIMATE and was in fact done: choosing N from an INDEPENDENT cost pilot that measured aggregates on separate random draws and never derived the hash order (disclosed in full below). Sizing a study from a pilot is universal and clean; resizing it after seeing its results is not. An earlier draft of this clause said 'may not be resized after any cost or outcome is observed', which read literally forbids the legitimate sizing too -- it is corrected here deliberately, because a clause that forbids something already done is one somebody quietly reinterprets later.

pilot_disclosure_a_cost_measurement_prec.why_this_section_exists: N=5,000 was chosen using a cost observation made BEFORE this document was finalised. That is legitimate sizing, but only if it is written down and checkable -- 'we did not do the bad thing' is worth nothing undisclosed. An undisclosed pilot is how a clean study becomes an arguable one, so the pilot is disclosed here in full.
pilot_disclosure_a_cost_measurement_prec.what_the_pilot_was: Two separate cost-measurement draws from the cohort, unrelated to this document's hash rule: seed 11 over 40 curves, and seed 23 over 80 curves. They exist only to estimate stage-5 cost.
pilot_disclosure_a_cost_measurement_prec.what_it_measured: AGGREGATES ONLY -- quartiles, mean, standard deviation, and projected total signature count. These fed the cost model (median 31, mean 1,283, ~6.4M projected for N=5,000, ~5.4 days) and the choice of N.
pilot_disclosure_a_cost_measurement_prec.what_it_did_NOT_do: It never computed sha256(SEED || mint) for any curve, never derived the hash order this rule selects by, never looked at WHICH curves the rule selects, and never compared any curve's activity against its selection status. N was chosen as a SIZE, from population-level aggregates, with the per-curve selection order unknown.
pilot_disclosure_a_cost_measurement_prec.why_that_distinction_is_the_whole_ballga: If someone knew BOTH each curve's activity AND the hash order, they could tune N to include or exclude specific high-activity curves -- N would become a SELECTION knob, not a size knob, and the leakage prohibition would be defeated through the size parameter. That channel is closed here because the two inputs were never brought together: the pilot saw activity aggregates but not the hash order; the rule fixes the hash order but reads no activity. The AST test (b) above makes this checkable in code, not just asserted in prose.
pilot_disclosure_a_cost_measurement_prec.artifacts: Versioned at research/b11f/pilot/ (committed 58ef4c9), with a README: rate_probe.py + its two result files (serial ramp and the 1/2/4/8-worker arm), sample_sigs.py/.json (seed 11, 40 curves), sample_windowed.py/.json (seed 23, 80 curves, cutoff-bounded). Both draws are fixed-seed so a reviewer reruns them and gets the same curves. Verified before commit: no credential, no credential-bearing URL, imports resolve via __file__ so they run from the versioned home. They are NOT collection inputs and MUST NOT become selector inputs. The README also records that these are a COST MODEL, not a finding (+/-29% at 95%, the 80-curve pilot's own error, not the draw), and keeps the corrected first-probe mistake on the record (a serial probe reporting 40 calls/s while measuring itself -- flat 171ms, 1/0.171 = 5.85 being the plateau it reported as the endpoint's).

representativeness.a_uniform_draw_preserves_the_population: Because the draw is uniform on creation identity and independent of activity, the sample's signature distribution is the cohort's in expectation -- the heavy tail included. The 11,102-signature tokens appear in the sample in proportion, not dropped; that is the point. Research on the sample generalises to the full 33,866-curve cohort with sampling error on the order of 1/sqrt(N).
representativeness.what_it_does_not_fix: A uniform sample of a heavy-tailed population inherits the heavy tail, so the realised cost is itself heavy-tailed -- see the draw below. Representativeness and cost-predictability are in tension here, and this rule chooses representativeness, because a cost-predictable sample would require selecting on activity, which is forbidden.

cost_is_a_draw_not_a_promise.the_projection: At mean 1,283 signatures/curve, N=5,000 projects ~6.4M signatures, ~130 hours (~5.4 days) at 13.76/s. That is a MEDIAN-of-draws expectation, not a guarantee. 5,000 is the largest N that clears inside a week.
cost_is_a_draw_not_a_promise.the_tail_risk: The draw is uniform, so a random 5,000 can pull several 11,102-signature tokens the median curve is nothing like. A single unlucky draw could push the realised cost materially above the projection; the honest statement is that stage-5 runtime for this rule is a random variable whose expectation is ~5.4 days and whose upper tail is not bounded by the rule, only by N.
cost_is_a_draw_not_a_promise.per_thousand: ~26 hours of stage-5 per 1,000 curves sampled at the mean rate. The owner sets N against that: ~1,000 ~= a day, ~2,800 ~= three days, each a median with tail risk above it.
cost_is_a_draw_not_a_promise.why_the_tail_is_not_capped: Capping realised cost would mean stopping collection when a curve proves expensive, which is selecting against high-activity curves -- the forbidden dependency, arriving through the back door. The cost is accepted as a draw so the sample stays honest.

relationship_to_the_frozen_studies.B19b_B19c_B19d_run_on_this_subsample: The exit-timing, capacity-wall and non-issuance-signal preregistrations were frozen against the full cohort. They now evaluate on this preregistered subsample. Their hypotheses and methods are unchanged; their statistical power is reduced in proportion to N/33,866, with wider confidence intervals that each study must report honestly.
relationship_to_the_frozen_studies.the_preregistration_chain_is_intact: A preregistered random subsample of a preregistered cohort, frozen before any outcome, is still preregistration -- the subsample was fixed before a single signature was collected, exactly as the studies were. No study was re-specified after seeing data; the population it runs on was narrowed by a rule written into the same clean state.

clean_to_freeze.stage_4_never_ran: signature_inventory has produced no artifact for this window. No inventory, no counts, no outcomes exist. This is verified by the absence of b11a_signatures.sqlite and the quarantine record showing stage 4 exited before writing.
clean_to_freeze.why_that_matters: The whole value of this rule is that it is chosen in ignorance of what it selects. That ignorance is real here and is not to be spent by reaching for activity as a key because dropping the quiet tokens is cheap.

what_remains_to_build.the_selector: scripts/b11f_cohort_subsample.py: a pure function selected(cohort_mints, seed=SEED, n=N) -> the N mints, plus a CLI stage that writes the subsampled cohort artifact stage 4 will read. Committed AFTER this document, separately, so the document provably precedes the code that reads it.
what_remains_to_build.the_pipeline_wiring: stage 4's --source (and stage 3's cohort output, or a new subsample stage between 3 and 4) points at the subsampled cohort rather than the full one. That edits b11c and its manifest -- a change on the far side of the re-attestation, owner-authorized, reviewed both directions, exactly as the cutoff fix was.
what_remains_to_build.tests_and_sweep: the selector earns, before anything runs, per the standing discipline: (a) the AST leakage test -- inputs are creation-time identity only; (b) the pilot-isolation test -- the pilot artifacts are not reachable as selector inputs; (c) the nested-property test; and a mutation sweep over all three.

status_locks.this_document_selects_no_curve_yet: It fixes the RULE. The selection is realised only when the selector runs against the cohort, which is a separate, later, owner-gated step. Freezing the rule is not running it.
